F-001.title: Assurance disposition lifecycle was incomplete
F-001.rationale: The simplified lifecycle has no optional-assurance PENDING/SKIPPED closeout contract; explicit Reviewer/Verifier transitions own continuation.

F-002.title: Git command arguments were not equivalent to Git-selected paths
F-002.rationale: Authority is based on actual Git index/history paths, including descendants, deletions, and both rename sides.

F-003.title: Coordination authority was not a first-class lifecycle transition
F-003.rationale: ASSURE permits bounded coordination-only commits after the source candidate without reopening implementation authority.

F-004.title: Candidate transaction and terminal transaction were not formally separated
F-004.rationale: The exact source candidate is assured first; later coordination-only history is separately validated before publish.

F-005.title: Contract parsers disagreed on the accepted specification format
F-005.rationale: Legacy specification/evidence parsers are not authority inputs in schema-v2 core; strict state/event schemas replace them.

F-006.title: Owner-authorized recovery had no runtime capability representation
F-006.rationale: Recovery is represented by explicit revise lifecycle transitions rather than parsing arbitrary Git recovery commands.

F-007.title: Frozen candidate can deadlock with stale Git index
F-007.rationale: The simplified model creates a candidate only from clean committed HEAD and returns to EXECUTE for source rework; no frozen-index materialization state exists.

F-008.title: Evidence producers and evidence validators can diverge
F-008.rationale: Durable free-form Reviewer/Verifier report schemas are not controller authority; exact candidate status bindings are authoritative.

F-009.title: Assurance invalidation is too coarse for control-plane self-modification
F-009.rationale: Rework, evidence problems, and scope changes now have distinct invalidation semantics.

F-010.title: Component tests were stronger than transaction-level E2E coverage
F-010.rationale: WB-003 adds a real disposable Git transaction from trusted admission through exact remote verification.

F-011.title: Self-hosting publication deadlock confirmed by WB-038
F-011.rationale: An assured source candidate can reach subject publication without reopening source write authority or bootstrap Git bypass.

F-012.title: Cooperative guardrails became repair-path blockers
F-012.rationale: Runtime adapters are thin structured-event normalizers; shell repair command grammar is no longer controller authority.

F-013.title: Stop-hook pressure can cause unauthorized lifecycle-state mutation
F-013.rationale: Stop/session-exit hooks are not lifecycle transitions in the new controller; close is an explicit controller operation.

F-014.title: A runtime may be unable to modify its own adapter
F-014.rationale: WB-003 is deterministic controller/Git harness coverage; runtime filesystem self-modification capability is an external rollout concern, not controller authority.

F-015.title: Runtime hook commands depend on session cwd
F-015.rationale: Target worktree and relative paths are derived from native cwd, not a fixed repository-root assumption.

F-016.title: Agent-facing operating documentation is materially stale
F-016.rationale: The canonical audit classifies this as documentation-audit backlog; WB-003 tests controller transaction behavior.

F-017.title: Maintenance Mode does not yet reach Git-native commit enforcement
F-017.rationale: The simplified normal path uses one shared policy through Git-native adapters and requires no Maintenance Mode.

F-018.title: Normal Git conformance cannot represent an inactive Maintenance Bootstrap commit
F-018.rationale: Trusted admission precedes planning/open; the new normal path does not model inactive maintenance bootstrap commits.

F-019.title: Bootstrap publication can be exact-ref verified without normal PUBLISHED_VERIFIED
F-019.rationale: There is no PUBLISHED_VERIFIED lifecycle state; publish verifies the exact remote ref then transitions ASSURE directly to INACTIVE.

F-020.title: WB-038 E2E baseline is not in the published remediation ancestry
F-020.rationale: WB-003 makes the deterministic transaction harness durable in the current remediation ancestry.

F-021.title: Unassigned finding identifier
F-021.rationale: The canonical audit source has no F-021 entry; the gap is preserved rather than inventing a finding.

F-022.title: Candidate transaction capability validation is applied too broadly to Bash input
F-022.rationale: Candidate authority is a controller lifecycle API; Bash text is not normalized into candidate capability authority.

F-023.title: Hard-stop command normalization may overclassify benign Git option forms
F-023.rationale: The shared controller no longer classifies arbitrary shell/Git command text for write authority.

F-024.title: Maintenance Mode audit provenance is hard-coded to WB-039
F-024.rationale: Maintenance Mode provenance is not part of schema-v2 authority; immutable admission_id and Work Block identity provide correlation.

F-025.title: Git restore/checkout revision arguments are misclassified as source paths
F-025.rationale: No shell argv path extraction is used for controller write authority.

F-026.title: Re-opening an active Work Block can silently replace its planning/evidence base
F-026.rationale: Open rejects active state and revise preserves immutable base/admission identity.

F-027.title: Stop hook can recursively block session termination while assurance is intentionally pending
F-027.rationale: Stop is not an authority-bearing event or lifecycle transition; pending assurance remains explicit without session-exit mutation.

F-028.title: Shell command segmentation loses newline command boundaries
F-028.rationale: The controller no longer segments Bash command text for authority decisions.

F-029.title: Shell tokenization loses quoted-separator provenance and can create false command boundaries
F-029.rationale: The bespoke shell tokenizer was removed from controller authority.

F-030.title: Shared hard-stop policy can classify dangerous command text inside benign task arguments as executable intent
F-030.rationale: Prompt/task argument text is absent from normalized controller events.

F-031.title: Orchestrator self-selected an Owner decision after explicitly pausing for authorization
F-031.rationale: This is an orchestration authority-boundary finding owned by later autonomous orchestration work (WB-004), not the deterministic WB-003 controller harness.

F-032.title: Shell grouping constructs can hide executable hard-stop operations from adapter segmentation
F-032.rationale: No grouping/subshell parser participates in controller authority.

F-033.title: Shell comments are not respected by adapter segmentation and can create false executable commands
F-033.rationale: No shell-comment parsing participates in controller authority.

F-034.title: Command substitution inside quoted argv data can execute hidden hard-stop operations
F-034.rationale: Opaque Bash is not converted to structured authority; command-substitution parsing is outside the controller.

F-035.title: Empty quoted words are lost, breaking shell comment semantics
F-035.rationale: The legacy lightweight shell lexer is not used.

F-036.title: Variable expansion can synthesize an executable command outside the supported grammar
F-036.rationale: Executable variable expansion is not interpreted by the controller because shell text is not an authority source.

F-037.title: Lightweight shell splitting is not a sustainable security boundary
F-037.rationale: WB-002 removed bespoke shell splitting from controller authority entirely.

F-038.title: Redirects to benign special sinks are treated as out-of-repository writes
F-038.rationale: Redirect targets from Bash text are not controller write paths; structured tools provide exact paths.

F-039.title: Canonical reporting-only inactive state is not committable
F-039.rationale: Schema-v2 lifecycle state is Git-private per-worktree metadata, so reporting-only INACTIVE state is not a tracked file that must pass commit conformance.
